title: Consumer-directed Medicaid support can improve care control and short-run satisfaction while long-run household recovery remains open
source_unit: ASPE Cash and Counseling randomized Medicaid consumer-direction demonstration
geography: United States; Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey Medicaid demonstration

observations.period: Cash and Counseling randomized follow-up; approximately nine months after assignment, study period 1998–2003

denominator.unit: adult and other eligible Medicaid beneficiaries in three-state randomized demonstration; state and outcome-specific denominators vary

intervention.value: random assignment to a monthly allowance and counseling for direct personal assistance versus usual agency-based personal care/home-and-community services

control_and_service_choice.value: beneficiaries could direct who provided care, when care occurred, and which permitted goods/services were purchased

service_access_and_satisfaction.value: treatment beneficiaries reported greater control and satisfaction, fewer unmet personal-care needs, and increased access to paid home care in cited comparisons

health_and_safety.value: cited summaries report similar or better health outcomes and no compromised health or safety in studied comparisons

long_run_recovery.unit: missing allowance receipt/spending, individual care completion, long-run health, caregiver durability, household finances, trust, switching, and exit

mechanism.value: A public program can increase service choice and short-run care satisfaction while shifting coordination, hiring, and care-management work to beneficiaries or families

observations.method: Structured extraction from ASPE Cash and Counseling randomized treatment-control reports; beneficiary service use, unmet need, satisfaction, and health/safety outcomes are kept separate from individual allowance take-up and long-run household outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: State-specific implementation and outcome universes differ. The public summaries do not retain individual identifiers, precise allowance receipt or spending, caregiver linkage, task-level need, long-run health, household finances, provider switching, trust, action, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Eligible Medicaid beneficiaries in Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey, including beneficiaries and representatives who directed personal assistance; no pooled beneficiary-caregiver household denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improved short-run satisfaction and reduced unmet need do not prove long-run health recovery, caregiver sustainability, household financial security, or durable institutional trust.

boundary: This record establishes a randomized consumer-direction-to-beneficiary-service-outcome segment. It does not establish completed care for every participant, long-run recovery, caregiver sustainability, or a pooled beneficiary-caregiver household result.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from published ASPE study reports; beneficiary, caregiver, Medicaid, and claims microdata are not retained.
